title: AI vs. Human Judgment of Content Moderation: LLM-as-a-Judge and Ethics-Based Response Refusals
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not analyze or measure any aspects of faith or religion. Its focus is on how human users and LLM-as-a-Judge systems evaluate 'ethical refusals' (responses that decline a prompt based on safety, legality, or moral concerns) versus 'technical refusals' (responses that decline a prompt based on system limitations).
findings: The paper presents no findings related to religion. The central finding is that LLM-as-a-Judge frameworks (GPT-4o and Llama 3 70B) evaluate ethical refusals significantly more favorably than human users do, a phenomenon the author terms 'moderation bias'. This divergence was not observed for technical refusals.
